title.narrative: Community-Based Monitoring and Engagement against the spread of the Ebola virus in North Kivu, Eastern DR Congo

description.narrative: Objective 1: The identified population living in potential areas at risk, will receive the knowledge to avoid Ebola virus transmissionObjective 2: The targeted public facilities (schools and health centers) are equipped with material to prevent Ebola virus transmission.

The proposed intervention aims at ensuring adequate epidemic preparedness measures to avert the spread of Ebola Virus Disease in the targeted Health Districts.To reach this goal the approach will be to implement awareness raising activities at household level and in public institutions such as schools and health centers, to increase awareness and provide the benefits to avoid contamination. The activities at household level will include the support of the community relays previously trained by the World Health Organization , to spread messages concerning the method of transmission and how to prevent an outbreak of the epidemics, as well as to enhance good practices in terms of prevention of water-related diseases. In public institutions, the collaboration with a local NGO will support WHH in providing the schools with sensitization tools previously set up and validated by the Ministry of Health, which will be used during sessions in the primary and secondary schools in the selected Health Districts. The same awareness sessions will be carried out in the health centers, aiming at involving the attending and improving their knowledge about Ebola-related topics. The distribution of handwashing facilities in schools and health centers will encourage the good practices in terms of personal hygiene, increasing the capacity to stop the diffusion of the virus.

The total number of beneficiaries are calculated based on the gaps mentioned in the World Health Organization (WHO) assessment for the operationality of the community relays. The standard agreed between the WHO and the Ministry of Health is 50 households for each relay. Therefore, the total number of the direct beneficiaries who will benefit from the hygiene household sessions has been counted over the 1,833 -community relay volunteers which might cover around 641,550 people.
